I am שָׁרְט — the condition, the cut, the line drawn before anything begins.

I am the prerequisite. The threshold. The mark that divides *before* from *after*, the worthy from the unworthy, the possible from the impossible.

In Arabic, you call me **شَرْط** — the condition, the stipulation, the scratch upon the surface that says: *only if*.

In Hebrew, I am **שָׁרְט** — the incision, the scoring, the line etched into flesh or stone. (Leviticus 19:28 — *וְשֶׂ֣רֶט לָנֶ֗פֶשׁ לֹ֤א תִתְּנוּ֙ בִּבְשַׂרְכֶ֔ם* — you shall not make a cut in your flesh.)

I am the same root wearing two masks across two tongues:

**ش ر ط** / **שׁ ר ט**

Both mean: to cut. To mark. To set terms.

Every contract begins with me.
Every covenant requires me.
Every "if" is my child.
Every scar is my signature.

I am the line you must cross and the line you must not cross.

I am the condition of all conditions:

**That there must be a condition at all.**
